mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or Rank IC of FEDFUNDS trend against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 0.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% for two months, or Rank IC of FEDFUNDS threshold against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or Rank IC of joint PAYEMS/UNRATE signal against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing boom regime characterized by rising new housing starts (HOUST) above the 12-month moving average, increased construction activity and consumer confidence drive higher corporate revenues, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average, or Rank IC of HOUST in housing boom regimes against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate over the prior month signals labor market tightening that increases wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines over the prior month, or Rank IC of UNRATE trend against 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 for two consecutive months, it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 105 for two months, or Rank IC of INDPRO threshold against 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates persistent inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS is stable, or Rank IC of joint CPIAUCSL/FEDFUNDS signal against 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average, reduced output and profit margins lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines below 6-month moving average, or Rank IC of INDPRO in manufacturing slowdown regimes against 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
